claims: BA.3.2 and Stratus are new, highly mutated Omicron subvariants.
As of March 2026, BA.3.2 and Stratus are causing a rise in COVID-19 cases in the US.
BA.3.2 and Stratus evade immunity from earlier infections and vaccines.
BA.3.2 has 70-75 mutations in its spike protein.
The 2026 variants predominantly cause upper respiratory symptoms.
Severe sore throat is frequently described as "razorblade throat" or sharp, intense pain.
There are high reports of sinus pressure and congestion.
Hoarseness or raspy voice is specifically noted with the "Stratus" variant.
Loss of smell or taste is still reported, though less common than in earlier pandemic years.
The 2025-2026 vaccines target the JN.1 lineage.
The 2025-2026 vaccines are expected to offer protection against severe disease.
Rapid tests are still effective for these new variants.
